saints.name: The Chair of St. Peter the Apostle
saints.title: Feast of the Apostle
saints.shortBlurb: The Church honors not a piece of furniture but the teaching office and unity given to Peter and his successors at Rome…
biography: This feast honours the cathedra, the teaching chair, of Peter: not a piece of furniture but the office of shepherd and teacher given him by Christ, who said, 'Thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church,' and with him the see of Rome, where he ended his labors in martyrdom.

The keeping of the day is very old: the Roman calendar of 354 already marks 22 February as the birthday of the chair of Peter. Rome long kept two such feasts, on 18 January and 22 February, tied to ancient seats venerated at St. Peter's and at the catacomb of Priscilla; later tradition assigned one to Rome and the other to Antioch.

In 1960 the January feast was struck from the general calendar, leaving 22 February as the single Feast of the Chair of Peter. The wooden throne preserved at St. Peter's, a gift of the emperor Charles the Bald to Pope John VIII in 875, stands enshrined in Bernini's great gilt-bronze monument above the apse.
saints.knownFor: The teaching office and unity of the Church founded on St. Peter.
